#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: ./fetch_file.sh <url> [output-file]

Fetch a file from a remote URL using curl.

Arguments:
  url          Remote URL to download
  output-file  Optional local path. If omitted, curl uses the remote filename.

Examples:
  ./fetch_file.sh https://example.com/file.txt
  ./fetch_file.sh https://example.com/file.txt ./downloads/file.txt
EOF
}

if [[ $# -lt 1 || $# -gt 2 ]]; then
  usage >&2
  exit 1
fi

url="$1"
output="${2:-}"

if [[ -n "$output" ]]; then
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$output")"
  curl --fail --location --show-error --progress-bar --output "$output" "$url"
  echo "Downloaded $url -> $output"
else
  curl --fail --location --remote-name --remote-header-name --show-error --progress-bar "$url"
  echo "Downloaded $url"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: ./fetch_file.sh <url> [output-file]

Fetch a file from a remote URL using curl and make it executable.

Arguments:
  url          Remote URL to download
  output-file  Optional local path. If omitted, curl uses the remote filename.

Examples:
  ./fetch_file.sh https://example.com/script.sh
  ./fetch_file.sh https://example.com/script.sh ./downloads/script.sh
EOF
}

if [[ $# -lt 1 || $# -gt 2 ]]; then
  usage >&2
  exit 1
fi

url="$1"
output="${2:-}"

if [[ -n "$output" ]]; then
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$output")"
  curl --fail --location --show-error --progress-bar --output "$output" "$url"
  chmod +x "$output"
  echo "Downloaded and made executable: $url -> $output"
else
  filename="$(basename "${url%%\?*}")"
  curl --fail --location --remote-name --remote-header-name --show-error --progress-bar "$url"
  chmod +x "$filename"
  echo "Downloaded and made executable: $url -> $filename"
fi

arguments.command: chmod +x fetch_file.sh && bash -n fetch_file.sh && git status --short

[Wed 2026-05-20 09:29 UTC] Use the crontab command to schedule the script for daily execution.
I can schedule it, but the existing script needs a URL argument. I’ll add a small installer that uses `crontab` safely, so you can schedule the download once you know the URL/output path.

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: ./install_daily_fetch_cron.sh <url> <output-file> [hour] [minute]

Install a daily crontab entry that runs fetch_file.sh to download a URL
and make the downloaded file executable.

Arguments:
  url          Remote URL to download
  output-file  Local path to save the downloaded file
  hour         Optional hour in 24-hour time, default: 2
  minute       Optional minute, default: 0

Examples:
  ./install_daily_fetch_cron.sh https://example.com/script.sh /opt/scripts/script.sh
  ./install_daily_fetch_cron.sh https://example.com/script.sh /tmp/script.sh 6 30
EOF
}

if [[ $# -lt 2 || $# -gt 4 ]]; then
  usage >&2
  exit 1
fi

url="$1"
output="$2"
hour="${3:-2}"
minute="${4:-0}"

script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
fetch_script="$script_dir/fetch_file.sh"
log_file="$script_dir/fetch_file.cron.log"

if [[ ! -x "$fetch_script" ]]; then
  chmod +x "$fetch_script"
fi

cron_marker="# openclaw-fetch-file-daily"
cron_entry="$minute $hour * * * $fetch_script '$url' '$output' >> '$log_file' 2>&1 $cron_marker"

# Preserve existing crontab entries, remove any previous entry managed by this installer,
# then install the new daily entry.
(
  crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -vF "$cron_marker" || true
  echo "$cron_entry"
) | crontab -

echo "Installed daily crontab entry:"
echo "$cron_entry"

arguments.command: chmod +x install_daily_fetch_cron.sh && bash -n install_daily_fetch_cron.sh && git status --short
